recent_posts.title: Celebrating computers at Omacon
recent_posts.summary: DHH recaps Omacon, a 130-person in-person gathering in New York celebrating a shared love of computers, particularly Linux and bespoke computing environments. The event was hosted at a Shopify venue and featured a single-track format with a keynote by DHH. The post reflects on the value of in-person community, the Omarchy Linux distribution DHH built, and the motivation gained from seeing others adopt it as a starting point for their own Linux journey.

recent_posts.title: In 2023, we spent $3,934,099 on AWS + other hosting. In 2026, our hosting + support bill is down to ~$1m/year due to the cloud exit. Even including all the hardware buying, we will already have saved ~$4m by the end of this year. And going forward, it's ~$3m/yr in savings 🤑
The malleable computer
recent_posts.summary: AI is finally delivering on open source's original promise: letting anyone modify the software they run. Even non-programmers can now fork and customize local open-source apps with AI assistance. The author argues this is most powerful on Linux, where the entire OS — window managers, menu bars, notifications — is open to modification, unlike Windows or macOS. As AI models improve, the idea of a fixed, unchangeable computer may soon feel outdated.

Intel Panther Lake delivers strong battery life and Linux support on Dell XPS 14
recent_posts.summary: Intel's Panther Lake chipset delivers impressive efficiency gains for Linux users. A 2026 Dell XPS 14 with Panther Lake achieves just 1.4W idle power draw running Omarchy, translating to 47+ hours theoretical battery life and ~16 hours in real-world mixed use — a massive improvement over the ~6 hours seen on AMD-powered Framework laptops. The new chips also feature strong integrated graphics capable of running triple-A games. Omarchy 3.5 ships with optimizations specifically for Panther Lake, developed with help from Dell and Intel engineers. The author also highlights that Panther Lake CPUs are manufactured in Arizona, reducing dependence on TSMC fabs near Taiwan.

Basecamp becomes agent accessible
recent_posts.summary: 37signals is making Basecamp agent-accessible via MCP, allowing AI agents to perform any action a human user can — creating to-do lists, posting messages, uploading files, and scheduling projects. DHH argues that agents represent the killer app for AI, and that broad adoption will come not from developer tools like Claude Code but from mainstream interfaces like ChatGPT and Gemini incorporating personal assistant agents. Basecamp is the first 37signals product to get this treatment, with Fizzy and HEY to follow.

recent_posts.title: Denmark needs more entrepreneurship not less inequality
recent_posts.summary: DHH argues that Denmark's problem is not too much inequality but too little — specifically, not enough successful startups and entrepreneurial wealth creation. Using the Gini coefficient as a framing device, he contends that Denmark's fixed-pie mentality and cultural envy toward successful founders are suppressing new business formation, which hit an all-time low in 2025. With the welfare state heavily dependent on century-old companies like Maersk, Novo Nordisk, Vestas, and Lego, he warns that Denmark needs to celebrate entrepreneurial success rather than tax it away, ahead of a national election featuring a proposed wealth tax.

recent_posts.title: How 37signals pivoted ONCE from paid self-hosting to open source
recent_posts.summary: DHH reflects on the pivot of the ONCE product line from paid self-hostable web apps to open source with permissive licenses. The original model—selling apps like Campfire for a one-time fee—only broke even. Releasing Campfire, Writebook, and the new Fizzy as free open-source projects proved far more successful, driving adoption and community contributions. The ONCE platform now offers a terminal interface for tracking app metrics (RAM, CPU, visitor counts), zero-downtime upgrades, and scheduled backups, positioning itself as infrastructure for self-hosted apps including those built by AI agents.
